text:
kevin-customer: Hey team — since last night our app hitting Redwood inference is getting intermittent failures. Most requests either 502/504 from our side or curl shows 'Connection reset by peer'. Happens across regions (us-west-2). Works sometimes then fails for a while. No recent code changes on our side. Any suggestions?

maria-support: Sorry you're seeing this — can you paste a short repro (curl -v) and any openssl s_client output? Also your VPC/region and the model route you hit. We'll loop in infra.

kevin-customer: Repro below. Hitting hosted endpoint in us-west-2.

curl -v "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACT" -d '{"prompt":"test"}'
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (54.186.XXX.XX) port 443 (#0)
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Certificate (11)
* TLSv1.2 (IN), TLS handshake, Server key exchange (12)
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS alert, fatal unknown CA
* Connection reset by peer

openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai
CONNECTED(00000003)
139638...: SSL_connect: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to api.redwood.ai:443
139638...: errno=104

kevin-customer: We also ran tcpdump and see SYN -> SYN/ACK -> RST sometimes. 

sam-oncall: That tcpdump pattern sounds like responses are being dropped/rewritten by a middlebox. A common root cause in VPCs is a stateless NACL that only allows outbound 443 but blocks the ephemeral source port on the inbound rule. NACLs are stateless so you need explicit inbound allow for the ephemeral range your OS uses. Can you share your NACL inbound/outbound rules and the OS ephemeral port range?

kevin-customer: Our NACLs were configured by security to only allow inbound ephemeral 49152-65535 and outbound 443. OS default ephemeral range is 32768 60999 (we didn't realize). Rules: 
- Inbound: allow TCP 22 (admin), 443 (ALB), 49152-65535 (ephemeral)
- Outbound: allow TCP 443 only

kevin-customer: We saw intermittent because sometimes remote server picked a src port >49152 but often used 35000 and that packet was dropped by the NACL.

lisa-sre: Yep that's the mismatch. When your client uses local port 35000, Redwood's server responds to dst port 35000 — if inbound NACL blocks 35000 that response can't reach the client and you'll get a reset/timeout. Two immediate fixes:
1) Expand inbound NACL ephemeral range to cover 32768-65535 (recommended). AWS docs: default ephemeral is 32768-61000 on many distros.
2) As a temporary repro, set your OS ephemeral range to match the NACL so all local ports are within 49152-65535: 

sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range=49152 65535
# Then re-run curl -v and verify consistent success

lisa-sre: We can also run a quick control-plane probe from our side to your NAT IPs to confirm. deploy-bot ran a probe and saw asymmetric resets when ephemeral ports were outside your allowed range.

deploy-bot: health-check: probe 54.186.XXX.XX:443 -> client 35012 reset after SYN/ACK (no ACK observed)

kevin-customer: Changed net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range to 49152-65535 and retried 200 requests — all succeeded repeatedly. Rolling this change to prod now and will work with our security team to widen the NACL as suggested.

maria-support: Great — glad that reproduced. To summarize next steps for your ticket: 1) widen NACL inbound ephemeral ports to 32768-65535 (or at least include 32768-61000), 2) prefer using stateful security groups for host-level instances (they handle return traffic), 3) keep the temporary OS tweak if you need an immediate fix, 4) if you see TLS unknown CA errors after network fix, send full openssl output and we'll investigate cert chain. Please confirm when NACL change is done and we'll mark resolved. :thumbsup:

kevin-customer: Will do. Thanks all for the quick help — appreciate the clear explanation.

maria-support: Closing loop here but tag us if anything else pops up.
